sanskrit: sa eṣa kṛṣṇo vārṣṇeyaḥ purāṇapuruṣo vibhuḥ āste harir acintyātmā krīḍann iva mahābhujaḥ
english: He is this Kṛṣṇa of the Vṛṣṇi clan, the ancient primordial being, all-pervading; Hari of inconceivable nature sits here, mighty-armed, as if at play.

sanskrit: eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca saṃhartā caiva sātvataḥ śrīvatsavakṣā govindaḥ prajāpatipatiḥ prabhuḥ
english: He is the creator, the ordainer, and also the destroyer, the Sātvata lord; Govinda, who bears the Śrīvatsa mark on his chest, the master of all progenitors, the supreme lord.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvemaṃ vṛṣṇiśārdūlaṃ smṛtir mām iyam āgatā ādidevam ajaṃ viṣṇuṃ puruṣaṃ pītavāsasam
english: Having seen this tiger among the Vṛṣṇis, this memory has come back to me — of the primordial god, the unborn Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person clad in yellow garments.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva bhūtānāṃ pitā mātā ca mādhavaḥ gacchadhvam enaṃ śaraṇaṃ śaraṇyaṃ kauravarṣabhāḥ
english: Mādhava is indeed the father and mother of all living beings; go to him for refuge, O bulls of the Kuru clan — he is the worthy refuge.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktās tu te pārthā yamau ca puruṣarṣabhau draupadyā kṛṣṇayā sārdhaṃ namaścakrur janārdanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, those sons of Pṛthā, and the twin heroes, best of men, together with Draupadī Kṛṣṇa, bowed to Janārdana.

sanskrit: sa caitān puruṣavyāghra sāmnā paramavalgunā sāntvayām āsa mānārhān manyamāno yathāvidhi
english: And he, tiger among men, consoled them with supremely gracious words of comfort, treating those worthy of honor with due regard as was proper.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu kaunteyo mārkaṇḍeyaṃ mahāmunim punaḥ papraccha sāmrājye bhaviṣyāṃ jagato gatim
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, again asked the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya about the future course of the world at the time of universal sovereignty.

sanskrit: āścaryabhūtaṃ bhavataḥ śrutaṃ no vadatāṃ vara mune bhārgava yad vṛttaṃ yugādau prabhavāpyayau
english: O best among speakers, O sage of the Bhṛgu lineage, we have heard from you the wondrous account of what transpired at the beginning of the cosmic cycle — the creation and dissolution.

sanskrit: asmin kaliyuge 'py asti punaḥ kautūhalaṃ mama samākuleṣu dharmeṣu kiṃ nu śeṣaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Yet I have further curiosity about this Kali age as well: when righteousness is thoroughly disrupted, what will remain?

sanskrit: kiṃvīryā mānavās tatra kimāhāravihāriṇaḥ kimāyuṣaḥ kiṃvasanā bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: What will be the prowess of men then, what their food and conduct, what their lifespan and clothing at the end of the age?

sanskrit: kāṃ ca kāṣṭhāṃ samāsādya punaḥ saṃpatsyate kṛtam vistareṇa mune brūhi vicitrāṇīha bhāṣase
english: And having reached what point will the Kṛta age return again? O sage, speak in detail — you speak here of wondrous things.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa muniśreṣṭhaḥ punar evābhyabhāṣata ramayan vṛṣṇiśārdūlaṃ pāṇḍavāṃś ca mahāmuniḥ
english: Thus addressed, that foremost of sages, that great sage, again began to speak, delighting the tiger among the Vṛṣṇis and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca bhaviṣyaṃ sarvalokasya vṛttāntaṃ bharatarṣabha kaluṣaṃ kālam āsādya kathyamānaṃ nibodha me
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: O bull of the Bharata line, hear from me the account of all the worlds as it shall be, having reached that turbid time.

sanskrit: kṛte catuṣpāt sakalo nirvyājopādhivarjitaḥ vṛṣaḥ pratiṣṭhito dharmo manuṣyeṣv abhavat purā
english: In the Kṛta age, the bull of Dharma stood firm on all four feet, complete, free from deceit and false conditions, established fully among men of old.

sanskrit: adharmapādaviddhas tu tribhir aṃśaiḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ tretāyāṃ dvāpare 'rdhena vyāmiśro dharma ucyate
english: But pierced by one foot of unrighteousness, Dharma stands in the Tretā on three parts; in the Dvāpara it is said to be mixed, standing on only half.

sanskrit: tribhir aṃśair adharmas tu lokān ākramya tiṣṭhati caturthāṃśena dharmas tu manuṣyān upatiṣṭhati
english: Unrighteousness occupies the worlds standing on three parts, while Dharma remains present among men on only a quarter of its former measure.

sanskrit: āyur vīryam atho buddhir balaṃ tejaś ca pāṇḍava manuṣyāṇām anuyugaṃ hrasatīti nibodha me
english: Know from me, O Pāṇḍava, that the lifespan, valor, intelligence, strength, and luster of men progressively diminish through the successive ages.

sanskrit: rājāno brāhmaṇā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś caiva yudhiṣṭhira vyājair dharmaṃ cariṣyanti dharmavaitaṃsikā narāḥ
english: O Yudhiṣṭhira, kings, brahmanas, vaishyas, and shudras alike will practice righteousness through deceit — men become trappers of Dharma.

sanskrit: satyaṃ saṃkṣepsyate loke naraiḥ paṇḍitamānibhiḥ satyahānyā tatas teṣām āyur alpaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Truth will be diminished in the world by men who fancy themselves learned; through the decline of truth, their lifespan will become short.

sanskrit: āyuṣaḥ prakṣayād vidyāṃ na śakṣyanty upaśikṣitum vidyāhīnān avijñānāl lobho 'py abhibhaviṣyati
english: Due to the wasting of lifespan, they will not be able to acquire learning properly; devoid of learning and wisdom, greed will overwhelm them.

sanskrit: lobhakrodhaparā mūḍhāḥ kāmasaktāś ca mānavāḥ vairabaddhā bhaviṣyanti parasparavadhepsavaḥ
english: Men, foolish and devoted to greed and anger, addicted to desire, will be bound in enmity, each wishing to kill the other.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ saṃkīryantaḥ parasparam śūdratulyā bhaviṣyanti tapaḥsatyavivarjitāḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas, kshatriyas, and vaishyas, intermixing with one another, will become equal to shudras, devoid of austerity and truth.

sanskrit: antyā madhyā bhaviṣyanti madhyāś cāntāvasāyinaḥ īdṛśo bhavitā loko yugānte paryupasthite
english: The lowly will become middling, and the middling will sink to the lowest position — such will the world be when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: vastrāṇāṃ pravarā śāṇī dhānyānāṃ koradūṣakāḥ bhāryāmitrāś ca puruṣā bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Hemp will be the finest of garments, millet the best of grains, and men will make their wives their friends at the end of the age.

sanskrit: matsyāmiṣeṇa jīvanto duhantaś cāpy ajaiḍakam goṣu naṣṭāsu puruṣā bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Men will live on fish and meat, milking goats and sheep when cattle have perished, at the end of the age.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ parimuṣṇanto hiṃsayantaś ca mānavāḥ ajapā nāstikāḥ stenā bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Robbing one another and doing harm, men will be non-reciters of prayers, atheists, and thieves at the end of the age.

sanskrit: sarittīreṣu kuddālair vāpayiṣyanti cauṣadhīḥ tāś cāpy alpaphalās teṣāṃ bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: They will sow medicinal herbs on riverbanks with hoes, and even those will yield little fruit for them at the end of the age.

sanskrit: śrāddhe daive ca puruṣā ye ca nityaṃ dhṛtavratāḥ te 'pi lobhasamāyuktā bhokṣyantīha parasparam
english: Even those men who are ever constant in the observances of shraddha and divine rites will, overcome by greed, consume one another's offerings.

sanskrit: pitā putrasya bhoktā ca pituḥ putras tathaiva ca atikrāntāni bhojyāni bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: A father will consume what belongs to his son, and a son likewise what belongs to his father — things that should not be consumed will be consumed at the end of the age.

sanskrit: na vratāni cariṣyanti brāhmaṇā vedanindakāḥ na yakṣyanti na hoṣyanti hetuvādavilobhitāḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas, reviling the Vedas, will not perform their vows; seduced by rationalist arguments, they will not sacrifice or pour oblations.

sanskrit: nimne kṛṣiṃ kariṣyanti yokṣyanti dhuri dhenukāḥ ekahāyanavatsāṃś ca vāhayiṣyanti mānavāḥ
english: They will cultivate in lowlands, yoke milch cows to the plough, and men will drive one-year-old calves as draft animals.

sanskrit: putraḥ pitṛvadhaṃ kṛtvā pitā putravadhaṃ tathā nirudvego bṛhadvādī na nindām upalapsyate
english: A son having slain his father, and a father having slain his son, will speak grandly without remorse and will not incur reproach.

sanskrit: mlecchabhūtaṃ jagat sarvaṃ niśkriyaṃ yajñavarjitam bhaviṣyati nirānandam anutsavam atho tathā
english: The entire world will become barbarian, without proper rites, devoid of sacrifice, joyless, and without festival.

sanskrit: prāyaśaḥ kṛpaṇānāṃ hi tathā bandhumatām api vidhavānāṃ ca vittāni hariṣyantīha mānavāḥ
english: Men will plunder the wealth of the wretched, of those who have kinsmen, and of widows as well.

sanskrit: alpavīryabalāḥ stabdhā lobhamohaparāyaṇāḥ tatkathādānasaṃtuṣṭā duṣṭānām api mānavāḥ parigrahaṃ kariṣyanti pāpācāraparigrahāḥ
english: Of little valor and strength, arrogant, utterly given to greed and delusion, satisfied with mere talk and gifts, men will accept the company even of the wicked — taking up with those of sinful conduct.

sanskrit: saṃghātayantaḥ kaunteya rājānaḥ pāpabuddhayaḥ parasparavadhodyuktā mūrkhāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ bhaviṣyanti yugasyānte kṣatriyā lokakaṇṭakāḥ
english: O son of Kuntī, kings of evil minds, intent on slaying one another, foolish yet fancying themselves wise, will at the end of the age be kshatriyas who are thorns to the world.

sanskrit: arakṣitāro lubdhāś ca mānāhaṃkāradarpitāḥ kevalaṃ daṇḍarucayo bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Failing to protect their subjects, greedy, swollen with pride and arrogance, they will delight only in punishment at the end of the age.

sanskrit: ākramyākramya sādhūnāṃ dārāṃś caiva dhanāni ca bhokṣyante niranukrośā rudatām api bhārata
english: Invading and seizing the wives and wealth of honest men, they will enjoy them without compassion even as those men weep, O Bharata.

sanskrit: na kanyāṃ yācate kaś cin nāpi kanyā pradīyate svayaṃgrāhā bhaviṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: No one will formally seek a bride in marriage, nor will a maiden be properly given; women will seize husbands of their own accord when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: rājānaś cāpy asaṃtuṣṭāḥ parārthān mūḍhacetasaḥ sarvopāyair hariṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: Kings too, unsatisfied and dull of mind, coveting others' wealth, will plunder by every means when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: mlecchībhūtaṃ jagat sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati ca bhārata hasto hastaṃ parimuṣed yugānte paryupasthite
english: The entire world will become barbarian, O Bharata, and hand will rob hand when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: satyaṃ saṃkṣipyate loke naraiḥ paṇḍitamānibhiḥ sthavira bālamatayo bālāḥ sthavirabuddhayaḥ
english: Truth is diminished in the world by men who fancy themselves learned; the old will have the minds of children, and children the understanding of the old.

sanskrit: bhīravaḥ śūramānīnaḥ śūrā bhīruviṣādinaḥ na viśvasanti cānyonyaṃ yugānte paryupasthite
english: Cowards will fancy themselves brave, while the truly brave will despair like cowards; no one will trust another when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: ekāhāryaṃ jagat sarvaṃ lobhamohavyavasthitam adharmo vardhati mahān na ca dharmaḥ pravartate
english: The entire world will be united in a single object — plunder — established in greed and delusion; great unrighteousness will grow and Dharma will not prevail.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā na śiṣyanti janādhipa ekavarṇas tadā loko bhaviṣyati yugakṣaye
english: Brāhmaṇas, kshatriyas, and vaishyas will cease to exist, O lord of the people; the world will then be of a single varna at the end of the age.

sanskrit: na kṣaṃsyati pitā putraṃ putraś ca pitaraṃ tathā bhāryā ca patiśuśrūṣāṃ na kariṣyati kā cana
english: A father will not forgive his son, nor a son his father; no wife at all will render service to her husband.

sanskrit: ye yavānnā janapadā godhūmānnās tathaiva ca tān deśān saṃśrayiṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: Those regions where barley or wheat serves as food — people will resort to those lands when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: svairāhārāś ca puruṣā yoṣitaś ca viśāṃ pate anyonyaṃ na sahiṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: Men and women will eat whatever they please, O lord of the people, and will not endure one another when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: mlecchabhūtaṃ jagat sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati yudhiṣṭhira na śrāddhair hi pitṝṃś cāpi tarpayiṣyanti mānavāḥ
english: The entire world will become barbarian, O Yudhiṣṭhira; men will not satisfy their ancestors with shraddha offerings.

sanskrit: na kaś cit kasya cic chrotā na kaś cit kasya cid guruḥ tamograstas tadā loko bhaviṣyati narādhipa
english: No one will be anyone's listener, no one anyone's teacher; the world will then be seized by darkness, O lord of men.

sanskrit: paramāyuś ca bhavitā tadā varṣāṇi ṣoḍaśa tataḥ prāṇān vimokṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: The maximum lifespan will then be sixteen years; thereafter men will give up their lives when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: pañcame vātha ṣaṣṭhe vā varṣe kanyā prasūyate saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāś ca prajāsyanti narās tadā
english: A girl will give birth in her fifth or sixth year, and men of seven or eight years will then procreate.

sanskrit: patyau strī tu tadā rājan puruṣo vā striyaṃ prati yugānte rājaśārdūla na toṣam upayāsyati
english: Then, O king, O tiger among kings, a woman will not find satisfaction in her husband, nor a man in his woman, at the end of the age.

sanskrit: alpadravyā vṛthāliṅgā hiṃsā ca prabhaviṣyati na kaś cit kasya cid dātā bhaviṣyati yugakṣaye
english: People of little substance will bear false marks of distinction, and violence will prevail; no one will be a giver to anyone at the end of the age.

sanskrit: aṭṭaśūlā janapadāḥ śivaśūlāś catuṣpathāḥ keśaśūlāḥ striyaś cāpi bhaviṣyanti yugakṣaye
english: Towns will be marked by gallows, crossroads by poles for jackals, and women too will be marked by disheveled hair at the end of the age.

sanskrit: mlecchāḥ krūrāḥ sarvabhakṣā dāruṇāḥ sarvakarmasu bhāvinaḥ paścime kāle manuṣyā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Men will become barbarians, cruel, eating everything, harsh in all their acts in that final time — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: krayavikrayakāle ca sarvaḥ sarvasya vañcanam yugānte bharataśreṣṭha vṛttilobhāt kariṣyati
english: At the time of buying and selling, everyone will deceive everyone else at the end of the age, O foremost of Bharatas, out of greed for livelihood.

sanskrit: jñānāni cāpy avijñāya kariṣyanti kriyās tathā ātmacchandena vartante yugānte paryupasthite
english: Without properly understanding the sciences, they will perform rites accordingly and will act according to their own whims when the end of the age draws near.

sanskrit: svabhāvāt krūrakarmāṇaś cānyonyam abhiśaṅkinaḥ bhavitāro janāḥ sarve saṃprāpte yugasaṃkṣaye
english: All people will by nature be cruel in their actions and mutually suspicious when the contraction of the age arrives.

sanskrit: ārāmāṃś caiva vṛkṣāṃś ca nāśayiṣyanti nirvyathāḥ bhavitā saṃkṣayo loke jīvitasya ca dehinām
english: They will destroy gardens and trees without remorse; there will be a diminution in the world of the lives of embodied beings.

sanskrit: tathā lobhābhibhūtāś ca cariṣyanti mahīm imām brāhmaṇāś ca bhaviṣyanti brahmasvāni ca bhuñjate
english: Overcome by greed, they will roam this earth; and brahmanas will exist who consume the property of other brahmanas.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtā dvijāś caiva bhayārtā vṛṣalārditāḥ trātāram alabhanto vai bhramiṣyanti mahīm imām
english: The twice-born, crying out in lamentation, afflicted by fear, tormented by low-caste men, finding no protector, will wander this earth.

sanskrit: jīvitāntakarā raudrā krūrāḥ prāṇivihiṃsakāḥ yadā bhaviṣyanti narās tadā saṃkṣepsyate yugam
english: When men will be fierce enders of lives, cruel, harmers of living beings, then the age will contract.

sanskrit: āśrayiṣyanti ca nadīḥ parvatān viṣamāṇi ca pradhāvamānā vitrastā dvijāḥ kurukulodvaha
english: The twice-born, fleeing in terror, will take refuge in rivers, mountains, and rugged places, O upholder of the Kuru lineage.

sanskrit: dasyuprapīḍitā rājan kākā iva dvijottamāḥ kurājabhiś ca satataṃ karabhāraprapīḍitāḥ
english: The foremost twice-born, harassed by bandits like crows, O king, and constantly oppressed by wicked kings with burdens of tribute.

sanskrit: dhairyaṃ tyaktvā mahīpāla dāruṇe yugasaṃkṣaye vikarmāṇi kariṣyanti śūdrāṇāṃ paricārakāḥ
english: Abandoning courage, O protector of the earth, in the terrible contraction of the age, they will perform forbidden acts as servants of shudras.

sanskrit: śūdrā dharmaṃ pravakṣyanti brāhmaṇāḥ paryupāsakāḥ śrotāraś ca bhaviṣyanti prāmāṇyena vyavasthitāḥ
english: Śūdras will expound Dharma while brahmanas attend upon them as devotees, and these will be the established authorities whom people listen to.

sanskrit: viparītaś ca loko 'yaṃ bhaviṣyaty adharottaraḥ eḍūkān pūjayiṣyanti varjayiṣyanti devatāḥ śūdrāḥ paricariṣyanti na dvijān yugasaṃkṣaye
english: This world will be inverted, with low becoming high; they will worship burial mounds and shun the gods; shudras will be attended upon and not the twice-born at the contraction of the age.

sanskrit: āśrameṣu maharṣīṇāṃ brāhmaṇāvasatheṣu ca devasthāneṣu caityeṣu nāgānām ālayeṣu ca
english: In the hermitages of the great sages, in the dwelling places of brahmanas, in temples of the gods, in sacred shrines, and in the abodes of serpents —

sanskrit: eḍūkacihnā pṛthivī na devagṛhabhūṣitā bhaviṣyati yuge kṣīṇe tad yugāntasya lakṣaṇam
english: — the earth will be marked by burial mounds and not adorned with temples of gods when the age has waned; that is the sign of the end of the age.

sanskrit: yadā raudrā dharmahīnā māṃsādāḥ pānapās tathā bhaviṣyanti narā nityaṃ tadā saṃkṣepsyate yugam
english: When men will always be fierce, devoid of Dharma, meat-eaters and drunkards, then the age will contract.

sanskrit: puṣpe puṣpaṃ yadā rājan phale phalam upāśritam prajāsyati mahārāja tadā saṃkṣepsyate yugam
english: When, O king, O great king, flower will germinate within flower and fruit within fruit, then the age will contract.

sanskrit: akālavarṣī parjanyo bhaviṣyati gate yuge akrameṇa manuṣyāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati tadā kriyā virodham atha yāsyanti vṛṣalā brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
english: When the age has passed, the rain-cloud will rain out of season; the acts of men will then proceed without order; and the low-caste will enter into conflict with brahmanas.

sanskrit: mahī mlecchasamākīrṇā bhaviṣyati tato 'cirāt karabhārabh ayād viprā bhajiṣyanti diśo daśa
english: The earth will soon be overrun by barbarians; out of fear of the burden of tribute, brahmanas will flee to the ten directions.

sanskrit: nirviśeṣā janapadā narāvṛṣṭibhir arditāḥ āśramān abhipatsyanti phalamūlopajīvinaḥ
english: The districts, undifferentiated and afflicted by rain upon men, will resort to hermitages, living on fruits and roots.

sanskrit: evaṃ paryākule loke maryādā na bhaviṣyati na sthāsyanty upadeśe ca śiṣyā vipriyakāriṇaḥ
english: When the world is thus in turmoil, there will be no rule of law; disciples who act disagreeably will not abide by their teacher's instruction.

sanskrit: ācāryopanidhiś caiva vatsyate tadanantaram arthayuktyā pravatsyanti mitrasaṃbandhibāndhavāḥ abhāvaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yugānte ca bhaviṣyati
english: The teacher's deposit too will be consumed thereafter; friends, connections, and kinsmen will leave for the sake of material interest; and there will be the disappearance of all beings at the end of the age.

sanskrit: diśaḥ prajvalitāḥ sarvā nakṣatrāṇi calāni ca jyotīṃṣi pratikūlāni vātāḥ paryākulās tathā ulkāpātāś ca bahavo mahābhayanidarśakāḥ
english: All the directions will be ablaze; the stars will be in motion; celestial lights will move adversely; the winds will be turbulent; and there will be many meteor-falls portending great terror.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhir anyaiś ca sahito bhāskaraḥ pratapiṣyati tumulāś cāpi nirhrādā digdāhāś cāpi sarvaśaḥ kabandhāntarhito bhānur udayāstamaye tadā
english: The sun, accompanied by six others, will blaze with fierce heat; there will be tumultuous roaring sounds and burning of the directions on all sides; and the sun will be hidden by a headless trunk at rising and setting.

sanskrit: akālavarṣī ca tadā bhaviṣyati sahasradṛk sasyāni ca na rokṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: The thousand-eyed Indra will rain out of season, and crops will not grow when the end of the age draws near.
